This Reva University Lab Inventory Management System is a fully-featured web application designed to automate all laboratory operations including equipment management, consumables tracking, maintenance, audits, vendor tracking, and student item requests.
The system is based on the modules present in your Excel file, ensuring a realistic and institution-level workflow.


---

🔐 1. Faculty Login Module

Secure login for authorized faculty:

Email (validated for Reva domain)

Password

Forgot Password (OTP / Reset Link)

Session-based access


After login → redirect to main dashboard.


---

🏠 2. Faculty Dashboard (Integrated With Excel Data Models)

Shows real-time overview based on:

From ASSET_REGISTER (Equipment Register)

Total Assets

Working vs Non-working status

Recently added equipment

Equipment requiring maintenance


From CONSUMABLES_MASTER

Current stock of consumables

Low stock alerts (below threshold)


From TOOL_ISSUE_LOG

Tools issued today

Pending returns


From STUDENT REQUESTS (Custom module)

New requests awaiting approval


Dashboard is styled with Reva University theme + logo.


---

📦 3. Inventory Management (Mapped to ASSET_REGISTER)

Faculty can view, search and filter the inventory.

Fields synced from Excel:

Asset Name

Category

Make/Model

Quantity (Total / Available)

Location (Lab/Room/Rack)

Serial Number

Vendor (linked to VENDORS_MASTER)

Warranty

Condition (Working / Not Working)

Last Updated


Search + Filters

Filter by Category

Filter by Working/Non-working

Filter by Location

Search by name

Low-stock filter


When clicking an item → open detailed view with:

Full Description

Purchase Details

Vendor info

Maintenance history

Audit logs



---

🔧 4. Add New Items (ASSET_REGISTER Integration)

Faculty can add equipment:

Item Name

Description

Category

Quantity

Price

Vendor (dropdown from VENDORS_MASTER)

Purchase Date

Warranty

Serial Number

Location


Added item immediately appears in inventory.


---

📤 5. Issue Items to Students (TOOL_ISSUE_LOG)

Faculty issues items to students OR approves student requests.

Fields:

Student Name

USN

Item Name

Quantity

Date of Issue

Expected Return Date


On issue:

Update ASSET_REGISTER available stock

Add record to TOOL_ISSUE_LOG

Link to Issue History


If insufficient stock → system blocks the action.


---

📥 6. Return Management (TOOL_ISSUE_LOG Updates)

When student returns:

Select issued record

Enter return date

Condition (Good / Damaged)


On return:

Update available stock

Update TOOL_ISSUE_LOG record

If damaged → update ASSET_REGISTER’s damaged count



---

🧪 7. Consumables Tracking (CONSUMABLES_MASTER + CONSUMABLE_TRANSACTIONS)

Consumables Master Includes:

Opening Stock

Current Balance

Unit

Refill Dates


Consumable Transactions Include:

Issue Date

Quantity Issued

Issued To

Remaining Stock


System auto-deducts stock & shows low-stock alerts.


---

🛠 8. Maintenance Log (MAINTENANCE_LOG)

Faculty can record:

Asset Name

Issue Reported

Date of Complaint

Repair Date

Service/Vendor handling

Cost

Updated condition


Dashboard shows: “Pending Maintenance” list.


---

📋 9. Audit & Verification Module (AUDIT_VERIFICATION)

Supports internal/external audits.

Fields:

Asset ID

Physically Verified (Yes/No)

Working Condition

Auditor Remarks

Verification Date


This ensures Reva University meets NAAC/NBA requirements.


---

🛍 10. Vendor Management (VENDORS_MASTER)

Stores supplier details:

Vendor Name

Contact Info

Address

Items Supplied

Warranty Support


This is used while adding new assets.


---

⚙ 11. System Configuration (DROPDOWN_MASTER)

Admin can configure:

Categories

Lab Locations

Item Status Types


This controls dropdown menus across the system.


---

🎓 12. Student Request Portal (New Feature You Asked For)

Students can submit requests:

Name

USN

Email (format checked)

Item

Quantity

Purpose

Expected Return Date


Faculty sees request with:

Accept

Reject

Reason for rejection


Accepted requests → automatically become ISSUED ITEMS.


---

📊 13. History Module (TOOL_ISSUE_LOG + CONSUMABLE_TRANSACTIONS)

Shows:

For equipment:

Student

Item

Quantity

Issue date

Return date

Status

Condition


For consumables:

Who took items

Quantity

Balance

Date


Filters:

By date

By student

By item

Pending only

Damaged only



---

👤 14. Faculty Profile Management

Faculty can update:

Name

Email

Phone

Password



---

🚪 15. Logout (Secure Session End)

Session destroyed + redirect to login.


---

🎨 UI Theme: Reva University

Official colors (Orange, White, Navy Blue)

Logo in header & login page

Card-based dashboard

Clean, responsive UI



---

📱 16. Fully Responsive Design

Works smoothly on:

Mobile

Tablet

Laptop



---

🧬 17. Final Outcome (What This System Achieves)

Digitized lab operations

Zero mismanagement of items

Accurate stock levels

Instant approvals for student requests

Transparent item tracking

Easy audits & maintenance tracking

Fast issue/return workflow

Professional Reva University lab management system

**Developing the Framework**

Okay, I've got the project's core figured out. I'm focusing on "Reva University Lab Inventory Management System" (RULIMS) and its main objective: a feature-rich web app for handling lab inventory, equipment, consumables, maintenance, audits, and vendors. I'm starting with a comprehensive view of the system's needs.


**Mapping Out the Modules**

I'm now diving deep into the individual modules, ensuring each aligns with the user roles and Excel data structures. I've sketched out the key areas, including the Asset Register, Consumables, and Tool Issue Log. The tech stack is locked in: React, TypeScript, Tailwind, and Recharts. Styling will follow Reva University's colors and be fully mobile-responsive. For the backend, I'll mock data services for this frontend project, using local state or localStorage. I'm keeping the Gemini API expertise in mind, but no immediate AI generation features are apparent in the requirements.


**Prioritizing Functionality**

I've refocused on the core IMS features, leaving AI integration for later unless explicitly requested. I'm building the system as is. I have the architecture and key features in focus, and I am avoiding scope creep.


**Refining Module Structures**

I'm currently working on the precise structure of each module, ensuring smooth interactions. I've broken down the design into clear components, like `Inventory.tsx` for asset management and `Consumables.tsx` for tracking. I'm focusing on user-friendly modals and forms, and laying the groundwork for data simulation using `mockDataService.ts` to mimic CRUD operations.


**Outlining the Core Features**

I'm now prioritizing the concrete modules: Inventory, Issue/Return, Student Portal, and Maintenance/Audit. I'm focusing on "Assets by Status" and "Consumable Levels" views, which will drive calculations from the data. The Inventory module will feature a table with filtering and an "Add Item" form. Issue/Return will have an item and student selector, with a table of active issues and a return action. The student portal will show their requests. Maintenance/Audit will get basic tables and forms. Styling is locked in: Reva University colors with a mobile-first approach.


**Integrating Data Context**

I'm now integrating the `DataContext` to share my mock database state, ensuring that the components have consistent data. I've defined the key data structures: `Asset`, `IssueRecord`, and `Request` in `types.ts`. I'm focusing on the data services to simulate a more realistic interaction. I'll maintain strict coding standards throughout this process. I'm focusing on data interactions with a `mockDataService.ts`. I'm starting from the core components of the system.


**Building the Core Views**

I'm now fully immersed in developing the front-end components, specifically focusing on the core views.  I've laid out the structure for the `Sidebar`, `Dashboard`, `Inventory`, and `Operations` views, ensuring they integrate seamlessly.  I've defined styles using Reva University's color palette with Tailwind.  I'm also paying close attention to prevent any potential infinite loops and ensuring strict TypeScript safety throughout.  I've also realized that I need to make sure the Student Portal is accessible.


**Enhancing Login Flexibility**

I'm now refining the login screen to include a "Student Mode" toggle. This simple addition will direct users to the student portal without requiring full authentication. It directly addresses the need for student request submission, as outlined in the project requirements. I'm focusing on simplicity and clarity in the user interface. I will be sure to add a test for it.
